# BSC (Bharat Steel Group) — Sales Call Knowledge Base (auto-distilled)

## Corpus summary

This corpus is a large concatenation of real call recordings, but only a modest subset are genuine **sales/dealer/customer calls** relevant to training. A substantial portion of the transcripts are: (1) internal payment/billing/accounting disputes (handling charges, debit/credit notes, "pay slip" proof issues), (2) logistics/transport/loading coordination calls with the plant operator ("Yuvraj Operator" series – coil cutting, diagonal thickness checks, sheet counts), (3) personal/unrelated Hindi-Gujarati chatter (the "Vishal" series), and (4) short voicemail/wrong-number/garbled snippets. These were excluded from the analysis below per instructions.

The genuine sales material that remains comes mostly from: Varsha/Vasudevan-type inside-sales reps fielding **rate enquiries and quotation negotiation** calls from fabricators, contractors, traders and engineers (TMT, plates, angles, channels, flats, sheets); a few **transport/freight rate** negotiation calls (Vizag Dushyant); and recurring **order-to-dispatch** follow-up calls (Sridhar/Vinayaga Steel/Vijayavel/Venkatesh patterns — confirm stock, confirm payment, confirm loading/vehicle). Given the mixed and noisy nature of the corpus, this KB is intentionally kept tight and grounded only in what's clearly said.

## Products & brand ladder

From the sales calls, BSC deals in long and flat **mild steel (MS) / TMT products**, largely traded/distributed rather than self-manufactured:

- **TMT rebar**: grades discussed are **500D and 550D**. Reps are explicit that in "sale"/CRS stock, only 500D is produced/available — *"CRS-ல 500D தான் sir வரும்... 550 வராது sir sale-ல 500D தான் வரும்"* [In CRS, only 500D comes; 550 won't come, sale only gives 500D]. Sizes quoted: 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 25, 32 mm.
- **Structural steel**: ISMB (I-beam), angles (L angle, MS angle), channels (C channel, I channel), square/rectangle pipes/tubes — though reps clarify limits: *"SHS நம்ம deal பண்றது இல்ல sir. மத்த item-லாம் குடுக்குறோம்"* [We don't deal in SHS; we supply other items]. Square tube is also explicitly **not stocked**: *"Square tube நம்மகிட்ட இல்லை sir."*
- **Plates (MS plate / checkered plate)**: thicknesses mentioned 2mm–45mm+ (2.3, 2.5, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16, 20, 25, 45mm), standard sheet sizes 4x8, 20x4, 2500x6300mm coil-cut sizes. Customers often request custom cutting; BSC generally resists cutting flats/angles ("Flats-லாம் நம்ம cut பண்றது கிடையாது") but will coil-cut plates to size for a surcharge.
- **CR (Cold Rolled) coil/sheet**: 0.6mm thickness CR per IS 513 was sourced via a known vendor rather than company stock.
- **Brands traded**: **Sail, Vizag (RINL/VSP), Vaisakh/Vaisakh**, JSW, Tata referenced as market benchmarks. Note: *"Vizag is not approved"* for at least one customer's site — a recurring approval/vendor-list issue.
- Company also quotes **transport/freight** as a pass-through service alongside material (own vehicles and hired trailers), with transport cost typically billed separately from material rate.

## Real rates & terms (only rates that actually appear in the calls)

- TMT 12mm: ₹69/kg, 16mm: ₹68.5/kg (quoted to Vimalkumar/Saveetha Institute, GST extra, "GST extra extra").
- TMT via Zetwork/Harish negotiation: base around **₹62–63.5/kg** (12–32mm), with 12mm sometimes priced ~₹500 higher due to coil-cutting cost; loading extra, "loading free" sometimes offered to close.
- Structural/plate rates referenced by VIGNESH A call: 8mm ₹67+tax, 10mm ₹66+tax, 12–32mm ₹63+tax, 35/50mm series also ~₹63.
- Plates (Vinayaga Steel Pradeep calls): running market ~₹61–64/kg depending on thickness (2mm ₹63, 2.5–12mm ₹61–61.5), later ₹62–64 with ₹500–₹1000 swings day to day; one call cites a ₹1/kg difference vs competitor "Kapil."
- 6mm MS plate (VR Earth Movers): ₹66–67 + GST, loading/transport extra, quoted via WhatsApp/quotation only — *"phone-லயே எல்லா detail-உம் கொடுக்க முடியாது sir."*
- Vizag CRS 20mm: ₹69,000 (per ton equivalent), loading free offered for a customer; sample policy = "1 meter sample = 1 piece only," must be collected in person.
- Odisha/general structural range cited twice: ₹65–67/kg ("structural plate-லாம் 65, 66 range"); TMT ~₹62–63 range in the same period.
- 45mm plate discussion: available stock size 2.5m x 5m (not full 10m length) — rounding to full lengths at ₹2200–2500/piece depending on size (Vijay M call).
- Vendor/distributor freight rates (Vizag Dushyant transport calls): Hyderabad–Coimbatore ₹3100/ton; Raichur–Chennai ~₹2100–2150; Vizag–Chennai ~₹2050; plant–Vellore/Katpadi ~₹26 (per unit, unclear denomination) with ~₹50-75 extra per additional plant pickup.
- Local haulage (Vel Murugan Eng): Trichy–Thuvakudi 15–16 ton = ₹1800; Gudur/Nellore AP 10 ton ≈ ₹18 (per unit).
- Standard **payment/handling charge** that recurs as a dispute point: **₹200 standard "payment charge"**, occasionally mischarged at ₹250 — customers push back hard on any deviation from ₹200.
- Terms: Many deals are **advance-payment-first, load-after** ("Cash and Carry" quoted by VASUDEVAN K: *"Cash and Carry தான் நாங்க எல்லாருக்குமே கொடுத்துருக்கேன்"*). Credit terms exist in some accounts (1-month credit mentioned in Vidveda Krishnasamy call) but reps are firm that **advance rate ≠ credit rate** — credit customers get a different (higher) price.
- GST is **always extra** unless stated "including" — reps frequently must clarify "GST extra" vs "inclusive" because customers assume inclusive.

## Objection Playbook

**1. "Loading/payment charge is new — remove it / why only me?"**
Customers (esp. long-standing ones) frequently contest the ₹200 "payment charge" line item as unfair or inconsistently applied. BSC's standard response: hold firm that it's a standard policy applied to all, tied to vehicle capacity — *"வண்டி capacity வச்சு அவங்க போடுவாங்க. நான் எதுவுமே போட முடியாது."* [It's charged based on vehicle capacity; I can't change it personally] — deflecting blame to "billing team"/policy rather than personal discretion. When a genuine billing error is found (e.g., ₹8000 transport charge omitted), the fix offered is a **debit/credit note**, not invoice cancellation (e-invoice/e-way bill already filed = cannot cancel).

**2. "Your rate is higher than competitor X"**
Standard move: hold the line firmly, cite "rate is final," refuse last-minute discounting, and reframe discount requests as disrespecting the quote process — *"நான் increase பண்ணி கொடுத்துட்டு கம்மி பண்றது எல்லாம் பண்ண மாட்டோம்"* [We won't increase then "discount" later as a trick]. Sometimes a token ₹500/₹1/kg match is allowed when a competitor's exact rate is proven (Vinayaga Steel ₹1 rate-matching episode).

**3. "Price is too high right now, should I buy less?"**
When the customer (engineer, repeat buyer) is wary of volatile steel prices, reps give **honest, consultative advice** rather than push volume: *"ரொம்ப வாங்காதீங்க... limited stock வாங்குங்க"* [Don't buy too much, buy limited stock for now] — building trust for repeat business over short-term order size.

**4. "Payment proof / documentation is incomplete" (e.g., missing vehicle photo during loading)**
Customer refuses to accept weak documentation (no camera/system proof). BSC rep initially deflects ("camera/system problem that day") but ultimately **concedes and offers a sealed, signed physical payment copy** to close the loop — shows escalation path: excuse → acknowledge → concrete fix (stamped/signed document).

**5. "Can you cut this length / custom size?"**
Flats and certain structural items are **not cut** as a rule (*"Flats-லாம் நம்ம cut பண்றது கிடையாது"*), though plates are cut-to-size for a surcharge (~₹5/ton extra cited). Reps explain **double-handling cost logic** rather than just refusing.

**6. "New/small customer asking for small quantity"**
Explicit policy disclosed internally: *"New customer-க்கு எல்லாம் சின்ன சின்ன quantity குடுக்குறது இல்ல sir"* [We don't give small quantities to new customers] — small/first-time orders are deprioritized unless referred by a trusted existing customer.

**7. Dealer/distributor price-matching pressure (Valli P / competitive intel calls)**
When a channel partner complains about low enquiry conversion or being underquoted vs rivals, reps are transparent about volume constraints: *"நம்ம ஏன்னா என்ன இதுவோ ஒரு சில சமயம் order-ஏ எங்களுக்கு கைவிட்டும் போயிடுது"* [Sometimes the order itself slips away from us] — acknowledging the real conversion funnel (~2 orders per 10 enquiries) instead of over-promising.

## Effective Lines (openings, discovery, closing, follow-up)

**Openings** — brief, respectful, state identity/company upfront:
- *"Hello sir, Good Afternoon. Sir, Narendra பேசுறேன் Sir, இங்க hashtag-ல இருந்து."* [calling from such-and-such company]
- *"Hello Madam, நான் Sangeetha Traders-ல இருந்து பேசுறேன்."*

**Discovery / needs qualification**:
- *"என்ன job work-க்காக use பண்றீங்க sir?"* [What job/work is this for?] — used to recommend correct grade/brand.
- *"Delivery location எங்க sir?"* and *"loading-க்கு tonnage/quantity என்ன?"* asked early to quote accurately (freight-inclusive vs ex-works).
